subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Great Debate of 1920
description: A fast breakdown of The Great Debate of 1920 for builders.

hook.text: In 1920, two astronomers publicly debated whether the Milky Way was the entire universe or just one of many galaxies.

buildup.text: Harlow Shapley argued the Milky Way was everything. Heber Curtis said 'spiral nebulae' were separate galaxies far away.

discovery.text: Edwin Hubble settled it in 1924 by measuring the distance to Andromeda—far beyond the Milky Way's edge.

twist.text: The universe suddenly became billions of times larger. Our galaxy was just one island in a vast cosmic ocean.

climax.text: Today we know there are at least 2 trillion galaxies. Shapley's Milky Way was a speck in an ocean he couldn't imagine.

punchline.text: One debate, one measurement. The universe grew a billion times overnight.

quiz.question: What did Hubble's 1924 measurement of Andromeda's distance prove?
options: The Milky Way is just one of many galaxies in the universe
The universe is shrinking over time
All spiral nebulae are part of the Milky Way

details.summary: The Great Debate of 1920 pitted Harlow Shapley against Heber Curtis over the nature of 'spiral nebulae' — were they gas clouds within the Milky Way (Shapley) or separate galaxies far beyond it (Curtis)?
details.whyItMatters: The Great Debate marks the moment humanity's concept of the universe expanded from one galaxy to billions. Proving spiral nebulae were distant galaxies revolutionized our understanding of the universe's size and our place in it.
takeaways: The debate asked whether spiral nebulae were in or beyond the Milky Way
Hubble's 1924 Cepheid measurements in Andromeda settled it
The universe expanded from one galaxy to billions of them

faq.question: Who won the Great Debate?
faq.answer: Curtis was right that spiral nebulae are external galaxies, but Shapley was right about the Milky Way's large size and the Sun's off-center position. Neither was entirely correct. The full resolution came from Hubble's observations, not from the debate's arguments.

faq.question: How did Hubble prove Andromeda is a separate galaxy?
faq.answer: Using the 100-inch Hooker telescope at Mount Wilson, Hubble identified Cepheid variable stars in Andromeda and used Leavitt's period-luminosity relationship to calculate their distance — about 900,000 light-years (later revised to 2.5 million). This was far beyond the Milky Way's boundary.
